numerical_failure.observed_behavior: When calling scipy.optimize.curve_fit with nan_policy="omit" and providing sigma, curve_fit raises ValueError("`sigma` has incorrect shape.") instead of omitting NaN-corresponding sigma entries.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: With nan_policy="omit", curve_fit should omit the corresponding entries of sigma where xdata or ydata is NaN, so that sigma’s shape matches the purged ydata size and the fit can proceed.
trigger_conditions: sigma is provided via the sigma=... argument
xdata and/or ydata contain NaN values (has_nan computed as any NaN over xdata/ydata)
the buggy version does not remove the corresponding entries of sigma when NaNs are omitted

input_output_examples.input: x = np.linspace(1, 10, N, endpoint=False) with N=90; sigma = x * 0.05; y = exponential(x, 0.2, 0.5) + np.random.normal(0, sigma, N) where exponential(x,a,b)=b*np.exp(a*x); then set x[11]=np.nan and y[22]=np.nan; call curve_fit(exponential, x, y, p0=[0.1,1.0], sigma=sigma, nan_policy="omit")
input_output_examples.expected_output: No exception; should fit successfully by omitting sigma entries corresponding to the NaN locations in xdata/ydata before shape-checking.
input_output_examples.source: issue#21772 repro trace and reproducer code

oracle_clues: curve_fit raises ValueError("`sigma` has incorrect shape.") when sigma is provided alongside nan_policy="omit" with NaNs in xdata/ydata (reproducer).

The fix is described as checking sigma dimension and removing entries where either xdata or ydata is NaN before determining type of sigma (diff in scipy/optimize/_minpack_py.py adds omission of sigma entries for sigma.ndim==1 and sigma.ndim==2).
PR description: bug is that nan_policy="omit" did not remove corresponding entries of sigma.

category_specific_evidence: Special values involved: NaN (has_nan uses np.isnan(ydata); regression test explicitly places NaNs into x and y and uses nan_policy="omit").
Where they enter: NaNs are detected via has_nan |= np.isnan(ydata); xdata and ydata are then purged using the boolean mask `~has_nan` (xdata = xdata[..., ~has_nan], ydata = ydata[~has_nan]).

Bug manifestation with special values: when using nan_policy="omit" with sigma provided, curve_fit previously did not remove the corresponding entries of sigma for the indices where xdata/ydata contain NaNs, leading to ValueError("`sigma` has incorrect shape.") (issue reproducer and PR description).

Correct handling: when nan_policy="omit" is active and sigma is provided, the code converts sigma to an array and omits the same indices corresponding to NaNs: if sigma.ndim == 1 then sigma = sigma[~has_nan]; if sigma.ndim == 2 then sigma = sigma[~has_nan, :] followed by sigma = sigma[:, ~has_nan].

Regression test coverage for omission behavior: test_curvefit_omitnan parametrizes sigma_dim in [0, 1, 2], constructs scalar sigma (ndim==0), 1D sigma (ndim==1), or 2D covariance matrix sigma (ndim==2), chooses indices i_x and i_y to place NaNs, then calls curve_fit with nan_policy="omit" and sigma (from the added test snippet).
reproduction_risks: Ensure NaNs are present in the data used by curve_fit: the omission mask `has_nan` is built using NaNs in ydata (and is also used to purge xdata), and the failing scenario is after setting x[11]=np.nan and y[22]=np.nan.
Use nan_policy="omit" (the bug specifically describes the sigma-shape mismatch occurring when nan_policy="omit" is used).
Provide sigma (the incorrect-shape error is described for the case when sigma is supplied along with nan_policy="omit").

Pick a sigma regime consistent with the reproduction: scalar sigma (sigma_dim==0), 1D sigma (sigma.ndim==1), or 2D sigma covariance matrix (sigma.ndim==2), since the fix slices sigma differently by sigma.ndim.
